title: Leibniz chain equation for assembled components
statement: For a scheme X, module sheaves F,G and a computing resolution pairing D, every assembled family of component maps satisfying the section formula satisfies the signed chain equation.

proof.text: Test the two maps from every total degree on each coproduct inclusion using HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor.hom_ext. If either integer bidegree is negative, its extended resolution term is zero; tensorLeft or tensorRight preserves this zero object, making the summand equality automatic.

For nonnegative bidegrees, use Mathlib mapBifunctor.d_eq, ι_D₁, ι_D₂, d₁_eq and d₂_eq to express the total differential as the sum of the left differential and the signed right differential. Precompose with the tensor of the two extension inverse isomorphisms and postcompose with the target extension isomorphism. Mathlib extend_d_eq transports the differentials.

Test equality on tensor sections using the sheafification adjunction and ModuleCat.MonoidalCategory.tensor_ext. The section formulas for tensorHom and the whiskerings compute the two source terms. The assumed formula hl, including its equality transports in degrees p+1+q and p+(q+1), identifies all three component evaluations with D.pair. Int.coe_negOnePow_natCast identifies the total sign with (-1)^p; D.leibniz gives the required equality.

proof_origin.place: construction before Lemma 20.31.3; direct summandwise Lean proof from Leibniz and extension by zero
